I have significant experience in deploying data engineering code encapsulated in a container at a cloud provider. It was quite good at processing GBs of structured and semi-structured data on a micro-batch basic. At the time it made sense to go this direction because the selected cloud provider did not provide serverless computing and reserving CPU/MEM ressources (VMs for Kubernetes workers) for the container was relatively cheap and easy to manage.
Lately I passed the Azure Fabric Data Engineer certification [(source)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/users/alexandrecagnon-1774/) to get my hands dirty on top of the shelf products from a major cloud provider. While Fabric is a powerful plateform, I feel that it has a too heavy cost overhead for small and medium sized projects. The certificate only covered some of the many possibilities of Fabric and Azure in general. One thing I really wanted to experience is serverless computing, more specifically Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) because of its potential for large cost and sustainability gains.

There are countless articles about creating Azure functions and an extensive documentation on how to from Microsoft. I'll take the party of fully ignoring any external documentation and only relying on Microsoft's documentation. I also use AI search (free Perplexity mainly) to help clarify some points. This strategy is used to reduce documentation swamping.
Also, I will iterate with only the most necessary additional configurations to reduce conofiguration complexity to the maximum. As the article show, a minimalist Function App already requires a heavy setup on your the local system and on Azure. This method should help cut through the *noise* of an extensive documentation and help deploy and run something as quickly as possible, a good start to iterate and build anything from. 
In this regard, this article is not a comprehensive guide but a quick start for someone who wants to create a simple Azure Function and deploy it to Azure. There is no intention to cover all possibilities, pitfalls and best practices on configurations, architecture choices, function choices, etc. That's more context specific and is part of the iterative process of learning and adapting for the specific use case.

# Hit Microsoft's documentation on Azure Functions

There's plenty of official documentation to work from as a starting point on [Microsoft's documentation on Azure Functions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/).

The [(Quickstart: Create a function in Azure from the command line)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/how-to-create-function-azure-cli?tabs=go%2Cwindows%2Cbash%2Cazure-cli&pivots=programming-language-python) is heavily used.

# Single Dummy Function Deployment

## Setup local development environment

## Install Azure Functions Core Tools

Follow the instructions [(Install the Azure Functions Core Tools)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-run-local?tabs=windows%2Cisolated-process%2Cnode-v4%2Cpython-v2%2Chttp-trigger%2Ccontainer-apps&pivots=programming-language-python).

Test installation success
```powershell
PS C:\Users\alexa> func --version
4.8.0
```

### Install Azurite

A Function App needs a *system* storage by default to function. Running Azurite locally allows to simulate a storage account for the Function App. Detailed [(Azurite installation instructions source)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-install-azurite?toc=%2Fazure%2Fstorage%2Fblobs%2Ftoc.json&bc=%2Fazure%2Fstorage%2Fblobs%2Fbreadcrumb%2Ftoc.json&tabs=visual-studio%2Cblob-storage) can be found in the Azure Blob storage documentation.

My short installation instructions on Windows are

1. Install Node.js from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/download)
2. Install Azurite with nmp
```dosbat
npm install -g azurite
```

Test installation success
```powershell
azurite --version
3.35.0
```

## Generate a new Function App template 

Using Azure Functions Core Tools CLI, generate a new Function App template in a directory of your choice.

```powershell
mkdir http_az_function_app
cd http_az_function_app
func init demo-function --worker-runtime python --model V2
PS C:\...\http_az_function_app> func init demo-function --worker-runtime python --model V2

The new Python programming model is generally available. Learn more at https://aka.ms/pythonprogrammingmodel

Writing function_app.py
Writing .gitignore
Writing host.json
Writing local.settings.json
Writing C:\Users\alexa\Documents\PRO_PROJECTS\http_az_function_app\demo-function\.vscode\extensions.json
```

The directory of the project is now structured as follows

PS C:\...\http_az_function_app> tree . /f

With my system's pyenv, the latest listed stable Python version is 3.14.3. ## Create a dummy HTTP triggered function

Let's create a HTTP triggered Function that takes an input *name* and returns a success message with it or a failure message otherwise.

### Create a function from template
From [(Function creation documentation)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/functions-run-local?tabs=windows%2Cisolated-process%2Cnode-v4%2Cpython-v2%2Chttp-trigger%2Ccontainer-apps&pivots=programming-language-python#create-func), we can use `func new` to create a new Function.

```powershell
(.venv) PS C:\...\PRO_PROJECTS\http_az_function_app\demo-function> func new --template "Http Trigger" --name helloName --authlevel "function" --language python
The function "helloName" was created successfully from the "Http Trigger" template.
```

The function was added to the function_app.py file as follows:

```python
[...]

@app.route(route="helloName", auth_level=func.AuthLevel.FUNCTION)
def helloName(req: func.HttpRequest) -> func.HttpResponse:
    logging.info('Python HTTP trigger function processed a request.')

    name = req.params.get('name')
    if not name:
        try:
            req_body = req.get_json()
        except ValueError:
            pass
        else:
            name = req_body.get('name')

    if name:
        return func.HttpResponse(f"Hello, {name}. This HTTP triggered function executed successfully.")
    else:
        return func.HttpResponse(
             "This HTTP triggered function executed successfully. Pass a name in the query string or in the request body for a personalized response.",
             status_code=200
        )
```

Adjust the settings of local.settings.json to test locally ?

### Test the function

As in previous local test:

- start Azurite with `azurite --silent --location azurite --debug azurite/debug.log`
- start the function app with `func start`. The newly added function will now be listed
```powershell
[...]
[2026-05-26T01:49:55.832Z] Worker process started and initialized.

Functions:

        helloName:  http://localhost:7071/api/helloName
[...]
```
- call the HTTP triggered function with the command (In PowerShell the native `Invoke-RestMethod` is used instead of curl) `Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://localhost:7071/api/helloName" -Method Post -ContentType "application/json" -Body '{"name":"Johny Doe"}'`
```powershell
(.venv) PS C:\xx\http_az_function_app\demo-function> Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://localhost:7071/api/helloName" -Method Post -ContentType "application/json" -Body '{"name":"Johny Doe"}'
Hello, Johny Doe. This HTTP triggered function executed successfully.
```

The function works as expected locally, let's now create a Function App in Azure to deploy it in Azure.


## Create the Function App in Azure

#### Install Azure CLI

To interact with your Azure account from the command line, install Azure CLI from [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/install-azure-cli-windows?view=azure-cli-latest&pivots=winget). 

**Test installation success:**
```powershell
PowerShell 7.6.1
PS C:\Users\alexa> az --version
azure-cli                         2.86.0
[...output truncated...]
``` 

### Create required Azure components

This [(documentation)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/how-to-create-function-azure-cli?tabs=go%2Cwindows%2Cbash%2Cazure-cli&pivots=programming-language-python#create-a-local-code-project-and-function)provides a list of required Azure resources to create a Function App before being able to deploy the Function App on our local system to the Azure Function App on Azure.

1. Create an Azure account on [Azure](https://portal.azure.com/)
2. Use/Create a Subscription on the Azure portal manually - here I named it `subscription_demos`
3. Login to Azure account and Subscription selection with `az login`
```powershell
PS C:\> az login
Select the account you want to log in with. For more information on login with Azure CLI, see https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2271136

Retrieving tenants and subscriptions for the selection...

[Tenant and subscription selection]

No     Subscription name    Subscription ID                       Tenant
-----  -------------------  ------------------------------------  -----------------
[1] *  xxxxxxxxxxxx_xxxxx   xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx  Default Directory
[2]    subscription_demos   xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx  Default Directory

The default is marked with an *; the default tenant is 'Default Directory' and subscription is 'xxxxxxxxxxxx_xxxxx' (xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx).

Select a subscription and tenant (Type a number or Enter for no changes): 2

Tenant: Default Directory
Subscription: subscription_demos (xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx)
```
4. Create a Resource Group (logical container for related resources) - `func-app-demos-rg` here
- select the best available region for the Function App (Flex Consumption) with this az functionapp [(command)](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/blob/main/includes/functions-flex-supported-regions-cli.md) - `southeastasia` in my case
- run the resource group creation command `az group create --name "func-app-demos-rg" --location "southeastasia"`
```powershell
(.venv) PS C:\...\http_az_function_app\demo-function> az group create --name "func-app-demos-rg" --location "southeastasia"
{
  "id": "/subscriptions/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/resourceGroups/func-app-demos-rg",
  "location": "southeastasia",
  "managedBy": null,
  "name": "func-app-demos-rg",
  "properties": {
    "provisioningState": "Succeeded"
  },
  "tags": null,
  "type": "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups"
}
```
5. Create a Storage Account (used by the Functions host to maintain state and other information about your functions)- `httpazfuncappsa` here.

**Register the Subscription to use Microsoft.Storage**
```powershell
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Storage
```

**Create the storage account**
```powershell
(.venv) PS C:\...\http_az_function_app\demo-function> az storage account create --name "httpazfuncappsa" --location "southeastasia" --resource-group "func-app-demos-rg" --sku "Standard_LRS" --allow-blob-public-access false --allow-shared-key-access false

{
  "accessTier": "Hot",
  "accountMigrationInProgress": null,
  "allowBlobPublicAccess": false,
  "allowCrossTenantReplication": false,
  "allowSharedKeyAccess": false,
  [...output truncated...]
  "type": "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts",
  "zones": null
}
```

6. A user-assigned managed identity (the Functions host uses to connect to the default storage account) 

The following commands creates a "Storage Blob Data Owner" role to the storage account (full access to Azure Storage blob containers and data) that will be used by the Function App to get access to the storage.

```powershell
$output = az identity create --name "httpazfuncappsa-user" --resource-group "func-app-demos-rg" --location "southeastasia" --query "{userId:id, principalId:principalId, clientId:clientId}" -o json

$userId = ($output | ConvertFrom-Json).userId
$principalId = ($output | ConvertFrom-Json).principalId
$clientId = ($output | ConvertFrom-Json).clientId
$storageId = az storage account show --resource-group "func-app-demos-rg" --name httpazfuncappsa --query 'id' -o tsv

az role assignment create --assignee-object-id $principalId --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal --role "Storage Blob Data Owner" --scope $storageId

#results
WARNING: Resource provider 'Microsoft.ManagedIdentity' used by this operation is not registered. We are registering for you.
WARNING: Registration succeeded.
{
  "condition": null,
  [...output truncated...]
  "scope": "/subscriptions/ef3c8ea4-a143-4356-8236-a2f08dc5a3a0/resourceGroups/func-app-demos-rg/providers/Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/httpazfuncappsa",
  "type": "Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments",
  "updatedBy": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "updatedOn": "2026-05-26T07:39:31.845940+00:00"
}
```

7. Create a Function App (provides the environment for executing your function code) - `httpazfuncapp` here

**Register the Subscription to use Microsoft.Web**
```powershell
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.Web
```

**Create the Function App**
```powershell
az functionapp create --resource-group "func-app-demos-rg" --name httpazfuncapp --flexconsumption-location "southeastasia" --runtime python --runtime-version "3.13" --storage-account httpazfuncappsa --deployment-storage-auth-type UserAssignedIdentity --deployment-storage-auth-value "httpazfuncappsa-user" --https-only true --instance-memory 512 --tags Environment=Demo

Creating deployment storage account container 'app-package-httpazfuncapp-5265228' ...
Resource provider 'Microsoft.OperationalInsights' used by this operation is not registered. We are registering for you.
Registration succeeded.
Resource provider 'microsoft.insights' used by this operation is not registered. We are registering for you.
Registration succeeded.
Application Insights "httpazfuncapp" was created for this Function App. You can visit https://portal.azure.com/#resource/subscriptions/ef3c8ea4-a143-4356-8236-a2f08dc5a3a0/resourceGroups/func-app-demos-rg/providers/microsoft.insights/components/httpazfuncapp/overview to view your Application Insights component
{
  "id": "/subscriptions/ef3c8ea4-a143-4356-8236-a2f08dc5a3a0/resourceGroups/func-app-demos-rg/providers/Microsoft.Web/sites/httpazfuncapp",
  [...output truncated...]
  "resourceGroup": "func-app-demos-rg",
  "type": "Microsoft.Web/sites"
}
```

Notes: 
- running `az functionapp create` automatically "created an associated Azure Application Insights instance in the same resource group... The instance incurs no costs until you activate it." [(documentation)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/how-to-create-function-azure-cli?tabs=go%2Cwindows%2Cbash%2Cazure-cli&pivots=programming-language-csharp#create-supporting-azure-resources-for-your-function). You cannot disable its usage by removing the  APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING from the Function App Environment Variables. if you want to reactivate it in the future you can always get the key back from the application Insights instance information in Azure. For more information on Application Insights integration with Azure Function App go to [(Enable Application Insights integration)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/configure-monitoring?tabs=v2#enable-application-insights-integration). An better alternative however is to use the user-assigned managed identity already created in step 6 for the Function App to access the Application Insights instance [(Documentation)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/how-to-create-function-azure-cli?tabs=go%2Cwindows%2Cbash%2Cazure-cli&pivots=programming-language-csharp#update-application-settings):
```powershell
clientId=$(az identity show --name httpazfuncappsa-user --resource-group func-app-demos-rg --query 'clientId' -o tsv)

az functionapp config appsettings set --name httpazfuncapp --resource-group "func-app-demos-rg" APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_AUTHENTICATION_STRING="ClientId=$clientId;Authorization=AAD"
```

- the additional parameters where added on top of the default parameters of the `az functionapp create` command provided in the documentation: `--https-only true --instance-memory 512 --tags Environment=Demo` for improved security, minimise ressource usage and better tracking of the Function App in Azure.

8. Upgrade Function App default storage account to user-assigned managed identity
Replace the default AzureWebJobsStorage connection string setting with several settings that are prefixed with AzureWebJobsStorage__ settings.

**Create 3 new environment variables for the Function App:**
```powershell
$clientId = az identity show --name httpazfuncappsa-user --resource-group func-app-demos-rg --query 'clientId' -o tsv

az functionapp config appsettings set --name httpazfuncapp --resource-group "func-app-demos-rg" --settings AzureWebJobsStorage__accountName=httpazfuncappsa AzureWebJobsStorage__credential=managedidentity AzureWebJobsStorage__clientId=$clientId

# results
[
  {
    "name": "AzureWebJobsStorage",
    "slotSetting": false,
    "value": null
  },
  {
    "name": "AzureWebJobsStorage__accountName",
    "slotSetting": false,
    "value": null
  },
  {
    "name": "AzureWebJobsStorage__credential",
    "slotSetting": false,
    "value": null
  },
  {
    "name": "AzureWebJobsStorage__clientId",
    "slotSetting": false,
    "value": null
  }
]
```

**Delete the old environment variable:**
```powershell
az functionapp config appsettings delete --name httpazfuncapp --resource-group "func-app-demos-rg" --setting-names AzureWebJobsStorage

# results
[
  {
    "name": "AzureWebJobsStorage__accountName",
    "slotSetting": false,
    "value": null
  },
  {
    "name": "AzureWebJobsStorage__credential",
    "slotSetting": false,
    "value": null
  },
  {
    "name": "AzureWebJobsStorage__clientId",
    "slotSetting": false,
    "value": null
  }
]
```

#### Create a .funcignore file

To prevent useless files to be pushed to the Azure Function App, we need to create a `.functionignore` file with the following contents:

```text
__pycache__/
.venv/
.vscode/
azurite/
.git/
.gitignore
.python-version
local.settings.json
```

## Check that the Function has been successfully deployed

```powershell
# Get functions from the Function App
$functions = az functionapp function list `
  --resource-group "func-app-demos-rg" `
  --name httpazfuncapp | ConvertFrom-Json

# Create summary table with correct property paths
$functions | Select-Object `
  @{Name="Name";Expression={$_.config.name}},
  @{Name="Type";Expression={$_.config.bindings | Where-Object {$_.type -eq "httpTrigger"} | Select-Object -ExpandProperty type}},
  @{Name="Route";Expression={$_.config.bindings | Where-Object {$_.type -eq "httpTrigger"} | Select-Object -ExpandProperty route}},
  @{Name="IsDisabled";Expression={$_.isDisabled}},
  @{Name="InvokeUrlTemplate";Expression={$_.invokeUrlTemplate}} |
  Format-Table -AutoSize

# results
Name      Type        Route     IsDisabled InvokeUrlTemplate
----      ----        -----     ---------- -----------------
helloName httpTrigger helloName      False https://httpazfuncapp.azurewebsites.net/api/helloname
```

## Run the Function from laptop

The [(documentation)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-functions/how-to-create-function-azure-cli?tabs=go%2Cwindows%2Cbash%2Cazure-cli&pivots=programming-language-python#invoke-the-function-on-azure) suggests to test the Function with the key from the Function. Note that it is not the best practice to use a key and store it in the code. A better alternative is to connect through the `az login` command without using key after the login.

### Getting Function key
Getting the API key.

```powershell
az login
func azure functionapp list-functions httpazfuncapp --show-keys
Functions in httpazfuncapp:
    helloName - [httpTrigger]
        Invoke url: https://httpazfuncapp.azurewebsites.net/api/helloname?code=xxxxx
```

### Run Function with key
Call the Function from the laptop using the Invoke URL template.
Note that the Function call with fail if connection to azure is not established.


```powershell
# with az login
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://httpazfuncapp.azurewebsites.net/api/helloname?code=xxxx" -Method Post -ContentType "application/json" -Body '{"name":"Johny Doe"}'
Hello, Johny Doe. This HTTP triggered function executed successfully.

# without az login
az logout
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://httpazfuncapp.azurewebsites.net/api/helloname?code=xxxx" -Method Post -ContentType "application/json" -Body '{"name":"Johny Doe"}'
Invoke-RestMethod: Response status code does not indicate success: 401 (Unauthorized).
```
